significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that per-item required concept depth increases with typological/script distance and low resource level, predicts cross-lingual errors, and crosses a fixed-depth truncation boundary under which extra computation restores the answer; it also includes the form-(ii) mechanism that "truncation — not missing knowledge — causes a large fraction of cross-lingual errors." This would establish both a quantitative phenomenon and a causal mechanism, fixing expectations across languages and distinguishing unfinished computation from absent knowledge—a consequential resolution given the layer-dependent multilingual processing documented by Wendler et al., "Do Llamas Work in English? On the Latent Language of Multilingual Transformers" (ACL 2024). True and false are determinate: a negative result would rule out distance-linked depth truncation as a substantial causal account, although it would not resolve all possible sources of multilingual disparity. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not earn this score; the specific scaling relation, truncation boundary, and knowledge-versus-computation decomposition are materially stronger than the median hypothesis about shared versus language-specific representations.

reach.justification: The claim names three usable handles: the per-item "required depth," the "Truncation Gap," and "adaptive per-item depth allocation" implemented by "looping the final transformer layers." Required depth is an ex-ante/online predictor because deployment teams could "route only high-required-depth items to extra compute" before committing the answer, giving auditors and deployment practitioners an action window rather than merely explaining completed failures. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted relation still predicts that deficits and recovery scale with typological/script distance and resource level; the hypothesis addresses multilingual LLMs generally and explicitly spans factual QA, reasoning, translation, and multiple model families, though the particular looping intervention may remain architecture-sensitive. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the topic alone supplies neither a routing metric nor a transferable depth-error relation, whereas these claim-specific handles support uptake beyond researchers studying multilingual representations.
